messages.subject: Re: multiple transition lists
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dorota,

When you used 'groupComparison' function,

ndbC.comparisons <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=xxx)

the input of group comparison, here xxx, is the list format, which means that it includes some data frame and other information. So, xxx should be the output of dataProcess. So, error message asks other information.

and after normalizing separately and merging together, dataProcess process next run-level summarization step. so, need to do dataProcess with merged data.

Here is what I suggest.
1.  I assume that 'ndbcvsWt_norm1C&2C_6proteins.csv' is normalized and merged data. Then reformat this data for MSstats input format.

tmp <- read.csv('ndbcvsWt_norm1C&2C_6proteins.csv')

tmp1 <- data.frame(ProteinName = tmp$PROTEIN,

                     PeptideSequence = tmp$PEPTIDE,

                     PrecursorCharge = NA,

                     FragmentIon = tmp$TRANSITION,

                     ProductCharge = NA,

                     IsotopeLabelType = tmp$LABEL,

                     Condition = tmp$GROUP_ORIGINAL,

                     BioReplicate = tmp$SUBJECT_ORIGINAL,

                     Run = tmp$originalRUN,

                     Intensity = 2^(tmp$ABUNDANCE))

2. run dataProcess without normalization
quant <- dataProcess(tmp1, normalization=FALSE)

3. run groupComparison
unique(quant$ProcessedData$GROUP_ORIGINAL)

comparison<-matrix(c(1,-1), nrow=1)
row.names(comparison)<-"ndbC-WT"

ndbC.comparisons <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=quant)

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena

We are preparing the manuscript about new approach of MSstats v3. In brief, imputation and TMP strategy in MSstats is more sensitive across several datasets. I attach one of results, with iPRG 2015 data. More details will be described in the manuscript. The paper, A statistical framework for protein quantitation in bottom-up MS-based proteomics, Y Karpievitch et al. Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena
